analyses.interpretation: Strength centers near 36 MPa with moderate spread; the distribution is right-skewed because strength grows with age, so the median and quartiles describe it better than the mean alone.

assumptions: two independent groups (dictionary: non-paired); independence assumed from design
analyses.interpretation: Group B shows a higher mean strength than A; the Welch test and Cohen's d quantify the difference and its uncertainty. Statistical significance does not by itself establish practical importance — judge the mean-diff CI against the engineering tolerance.

Strength increases with age; Pearson r and its Fisher-z CI summarize the linear association. This is association, not causation, and the relation is curved (log-like), so r understates the monotonic trend — Spearman would be higher.

The OLS line gives an average strength gain per day of age with R² indicating fit; the slope CI expresses uncertainty. A linear model is an approximation of a saturating growth curve — inspect residuals before extrapolating.
